about.vision.paragraph1: OSHI is not just a messenger — it's a **communication protocol for digital freedom**. Built on principles of sovereignty, privacy, and resilience.
about.vision.paragraph2: When someone is in range, OSHI works **with no internet and no server at all**, routing messages over **peer-to-peer mesh networking** through direct Bluetooth/Wi-Fi links or multi-hop relays. When nobody is in range, it falls back to our relay so the message still arrives.

desktop.media.caveat.animated: Animated — the first frame is shown. This window has no animation loop; playing it would need a frame clock this viewer deliberately does not have.
desktop.media.caveat.truncated: Incomplete: this file does not end the way its format requires, so part of the picture is missing and what fills that space was never sent. A download that was interrupted, or a copy that was. Ask the sender to send it again.
desktop.media.caveat.view_once: View once: you have opened this. The file stays on this disk — this client does not destroy it and the sender is never told — and it is not revealed in your file manager from here.
desktop.media.no_key: No media key is loaded in this window, so the attachment cannot be decrypted.
desktop.media.note.empty: The file on disk is zero bytes. That is a failed or interrupted write here, not a damaged message — the download deletes a partial file, so an empty one means the path was created by something else.
desktop.media.note.inline_oversize: This image is too large for this window to decode in one piece (over 16 MiB). The file is on disk and intact; open it in an image viewer.
desktop.media.note.missing_file: The decrypted file is not at that path any more. Nothing was lost on the wire — the bytes were written to this disk when the message arrived and something has removed them since.
desktop.media.note.no_header: This file does not begin with an image header this window can read — truncated at the very start, or not a picture at all whatever it is called. Nothing was decoded, because there were no dimensions to decode into.
desktop.media.note.not_a_file: There is no file at that path any more. The bytes were decrypted to this disk when the message arrived; something has removed or moved them since. Nothing was lost on the wire and the sender does not need to resend for this window's sake.
desktop.media.note.not_image: These bytes are %@, which is not a still image, whatever the file is called — the name came from the sender and this is what the file itself says. This window draws still pictures and does not play anything, so there is nothing honest for it to show. The file is on disk and unchanged.
desktop.media.note.oversize: This file is %1$@, over this window's %2$@ ceiling for reading an image into memory in one piece. The file is on disk and intact; open it in an image viewer, which can decode it without holding all of it.
desktop.media.note.sealed: View once, as the sender marked it. Reveal is a LOCAL action: this client does not destroy the file afterwards and the sender is never told you opened it.
desktop.media.note.too_many_pixels: This image declares %1$@ — %2$@ megapixels, over this window's %3$@ MP decoding ceiling. Nothing was decoded: the dimensions come from the file's header. A small file that claims enormous dimensions is the shape of a deliberate attack as well as the shape of a panorama, and this window declines both the same way.
desktop.media.note.undecodable: The bytes are on disk but this window's image library could not turn them into a picture. Truncated, or a format this build of skia does not carry. That is a statement about THIS decoder and not about the file: another OSHI client, and your own image viewer, may well open it.
desktop.media.note.unparseable: This attachment reference is not in the form this window knows how to read, so it is shown verbatim rather than interpreted.

guide.add_contact.s1: Tap the + button, then "My code". That QR code IS your address in OSHI. There is no phone number and no username.
guide.add_contact.s2: Sitting together? Have them tap "Scan" and point their camera at your code. You are connected — that is the whole step.
guide.add_contact.s3: Far apart? Tap "Invite by link" and send that link however you like — SMS, email, any app. Opening it on a phone with OSHI adds you.
guide.add_contact.s4: No internet at all? Open "Nearby". Any phone running OSHI within about 100 m appears there over Bluetooth, and you can add each other with no network.
guide.add_contact.title: Add a contact
guide.cashu.s1: OSHI has no wallet and never holds your money. It carries a Cashu token — ecash backed by bitcoin — the way it carries a photo.
guide.cashu.s2: You need a Cashu wallet first. eNuts, Minibits, or cashu.me in a browser: all free, about a minute to set up.
guide.cashu.s3: In the wallet, choose a mint and add a little money over Lightning. A few hundred sats is plenty to try this.
guide.cashu.s4: Make a token: tap Send in the wallet, enter an amount, copy. You get a long line of text starting with cashuB. That text IS the money.
guide.cashu.s5: In the chat, type / in the message box and choose /pay, then paste the token. OSHI shows the amount before it sends, so you can check it.
guide.cashu.s6: They tap Redeem and the money lands in their wallet. A token sent to you looks the same: tap Redeem. OSHI is only the envelope.
guide.cashu.sub: Cashu ecash — OSHI never holds your money
guide.cashu.title: Send bitcoin in a chat
guide.cashu.warning: A Cashu token is cash. Anyone who gets the text can spend it, and whoever redeems it first keeps it — so send it only to the person you mean. OSHI cannot ask the mint whether a token has already been spent: it is yours only once your own wallet redeems it.
guide_collaborative_desc: OSHI is collaborative: when you keep the app open, your device helps relay messages for other people nearby. In crisis situations (war, internet shutdown), this creates a resilient network. Each phone reaches about 100 m, so the more people with OSHI open, the further messages can travel.
guide_complete_desc: You're all set! Remember: keep OSHI open to receive messages and help others communicate in emergencies. Welcome to the network!
guide_groups_tab_desc: Create private groups or join public ones nearby. Discover groups within mesh range, about 100 m, and further when others relay. Keep the app open to detect groups around you!
guide_messages_tab_desc: Your private conversations appear here. Make encrypted voice calls by tapping any conversation. Messages and calls only arrive when the app is open for 2+ seconds - this is by design for security.
guide_new_tab_desc: Start a new conversation here. Scan a contact's QR code or paste their public key. No phone numbers, no accounts - just cryptographic keys.
guide_settings_tab_desc: Your crypto identity lives here. Share your QR code or public key with others so they can message you. You can also enable biometric lock for extra security.
guide_welcome_desc: OSHI is a collaborative encrypted messenger. Without internet, messages hop from phone to phone through people nearby who have OSHI open. Let's show you around.

keyboardPrivacy.intro: What you type passes through the keyboard before OSHI encrypts it on your device. Here is what OSHI can and cannot do about it.
keyboardPrivacy.limits.dictation: Dictation. Depending on your device and language, your voice may be sent to Apple to be transcribed. Type instead if that matters to you.
keyboardPrivacy.limits.jailbreak: Jailbroken or modified devices. OSHI looks for common signs of a jailbreak and warns you if it finds them, but the check can be fooled: no warning does not mean your device is safe.
keyboardPrivacy.limits.spyware: A compromised phone. Spyware can see the screen and keystrokes before any app encrypts them. Keep iOS up to date, and turn on Lockdown Mode if you are at risk.
keyboardPrivacy.limits.systemKeyboard: The system keyboard. It is part of iOS: OSHI cannot inspect or replace it and relies on Apple’s protections.
keyboardPrivacy.protected.clipboard: When you copy a message, a recovery key or a bot token, it stays on this device (it is not shared with your other Apple devices) and is removed from the clipboard after 60 seconds. Until then, apps you open can read it. Text you select and copy yourself (for example in OSHI Mail) uses the normal clipboard.
keyboardPrivacy.protected.encryption: Chats and calls are encrypted on your device before they are sent. OSHI Mail works like normal email: the mail server can read what you write.
keyboardPrivacy.protected.learning: With Private typing on, autocorrect, predictions and spell check are off in message fields, which limits what the keyboard can learn from your conversations.
keyboardPrivacy.protected.screen: Screenshots and screen recordings of OSHI show the OSHI logo instead of your conversations.
keyboardPrivacy.protected.thirdParty: Third-party keyboards are blocked inside OSHI, so a keyboard app cannot read what you type here.

lora.guide.footer: Once paired, OSHI uses the node by itself: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi first for whoever is close, LoRa when nobody is. Expect a few kilometres in a city, and considerably more with height and open ground.
lora.guide.step1: Get a supported board: a Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3, a Heltec Wireless Tracker or a LILYGO T3-S3.
lora.guide.step2: On a computer, open oshi-messenger.com/lora/flash in Chrome or Edge, plug the board in by USB and flash it. It takes about a minute.
lora.guide.step3: Unplug it, switch it on and keep it near your phone.
lora.guide.step4: Tap it under Nearby nodes above. You pair it once.
lora.guide.step5: Choose the region it will be used in. Until you do, the node listens but never transmits.

onboarding_disclaimer_anonymous_desc: OSHI is 100% designed for total anonymity. No accounts, no phone numbers, no tracking. Your identity stays yours.
onboarding_disclaimer_audit_desc: This app has not undergone a professional security audit. While we use strong encryption, use at your own discretion.
onboarding_disclaimer_cloud_desc: When contacts are not nearby, messages are stored encrypted on our servers and voice calls go through our relay server. Message content stays end-to-end encrypted, but group names and member lists are visible to our servers.
onboarding_disclaimer_critical_desc: Designed for scenarios when a country is disconnected from the internet. Communicate freely even when networks are down.
onboarding_disclaimer_mesh_desc: Send messages and make calls with no internet, phone to phone. About 100 m directly, and further only when other people nearby have OSHI open to relay. Both phones need the app open.
onboarding_disclaimer_note: Your one-to-one messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted. No phone number or account required.
onboarding_disclaimer_notifications_desc: For security, messages and calls are only received when the app is open. In crisis situations (war, kidnapping), if your phone is locked or the app is password-protected, notifications only arrive after the app is open for 2+ seconds. Keeping the app open also lets your phone relay messages for other people nearby.

pc.ledger.bots.title: Bot channels
pc.ledger.bots.why: Bot channels are not encrypted at all, so this window gives them no text box. They can be used from the command console (/bot send), which repeats that warning on every send.
pc.ledger.bubbles.title: Bubble styles and link previews
pc.ledger.bubbles.why: Chat wallpapers exist and stay on this computer. Phones keep bubble styles on each device and never sync them, so a style chosen here would not show there. A link preview would make this app open a link a stranger sent, which reveals you to that website, so it is not done.
pc.ledger.calls.title: Calls to a phone
pc.ledger.calls.why: Voice and video calls work in this window and were measured live between two computers, also through a relay server. A call to an iPhone or an Android phone has not been tested yet, and neither has a call across a home router. The speaker was checked on a real machine; the microphone is deliberately not tested automatically.
pc.ledger.checkpoint.title: Sync checkpoint
pc.ledger.checkpoint.why: Pushing and pulling the contact archive is under Account. A sync checkpoint stays in the command console because it deletes items on the server that your other devices may not have fetched yet. Scheduled messages, the radio and account deletion all have their own screens.
pc.ledger.controls.title: Reactions, edits, receipts and typing
pc.ledger.controls.why: Reactions, edits and deletions you receive are shown, and you can react, and edit or delete your own messages. Opening a conversation sends a read receipt when your privacy settings allow it, and typing is shown in both directions.
pc.ledger.groupAdmin.title: Advanced group administration
pc.ledger.groupAdmin.why: Sending to groups, creating, renaming, leaving, adding and removing members and changing roles all work here. The creator role cannot be given away. Rarer operations are only in the command console (/group) for now.
pc.ledger.languages.title: Languages
pc.ledger.languages.why: The app ships in 34 languages, and every sentence this window shows is translated into each of them.
pc.ledger.location.title: Sending your location or a check-in
pc.ledger.location.why: A computer has no GPS and OSHI does not fake one, so locations and check-ins can be received here but not sent. Places search works offline from maps on this disk, and contact cards do send. Over a LoRa radio, this computer can announce a position you type in.
pc.ledger.loraBluetooth.title: Pairing a LoRa radio over Bluetooth
pc.ledger.loraBluetooth.why: The desktop runtime has no Bluetooth. Connect the radio with a USB cable (macOS, Linux) or over the network (TCP port 4403); on Windows, use the network. Reading radio and nearby messages does work: OSHI messages are decrypted and filed under their sender, and plain Meshtastic text gets its own thread marked unverified.
pc.ledger.media.title: Pictures, voice notes and videos
pc.ledger.media.why: Photos open as a thumbnail and full size, with their format and size read from the file itself. Limits of 64 MiB and 32 megapixels keep a stranger's file from exhausting memory, and a cut-off file is shown and labelled incomplete. Voice notes and videos play here; playback through a real speaker has not been tested automatically.
pc.ledger.phoneSync.title: Syncing history with your phone
pc.ledger.phoneSync.why: A new desktop profile can restore your identity from your phone's recovery key, but message history and groups do not come across yet: the phones do not write the signed archive this app requires. The older, unsigned archive is deliberately not used.
pc.ledger.push.title: Push notifications
pc.ledger.push.why: Computers have no Apple or Google push service for OSHI. OSHI checks for messages while it runs, so nothing arrives while the computer sleeps, and the time between checks is the delay.
pc.ledger.screenshot.title: Blocking screenshots
pc.ledger.screenshot.why: macOS and Windows have a setting for it and Linux has none, but on macOS 15 and later screen recorders are reported to capture protected windows anyway. A switch promising a protection that does not hold would be a false security promise, so none is offered.
pc.ledger.watch.title: Apple Watch
pc.ledger.watch.why: A watch needs a paired iPhone. Nothing equivalent exists for a computer.
pc.limits.bluetooth.title: Pairing a radio over Bluetooth
pc.limits.bluetooth.why: The desktop runtime has no Bluetooth. Connect the radio with a USB cable (macOS, Linux) or over the network (all systems).
pc.limits.camera.title: Scanning a QR code with the camera
pc.limits.camera.why: Not every computer has a camera. Open a picture or screenshot of the code instead, or paste its text.
pc.limits.gps.title: Your location and check-ins
pc.limits.gps.why: A computer has no GPS, and OSHI does not guess your position from Wi-Fi or your IP address. Locations you receive still show; a radio can announce a position you type in.

pc.limits.nearby.title: Finding people nearby without a network
pc.limits.nearby.why: Phones find each other over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct. A computer finds OSHI devices on the same network, or reaches them through a LoRa radio.
pc.limits.push.title: Notifications while OSHI is closed
pc.limits.push.why: Phones are woken by Apple and Google push services; computers have no equivalent for OSHI. Messages arrive while OSHI runs, also from the menu bar or tray, and are waiting when you open it.
pc.limits.screenshot.title: Blocking screenshots
pc.limits.screenshot.why: No system offers it reliably: Linux has no way at all, and on recent macOS screen recorders can still capture a protected window. A switch that promised it would be a false promise.

welcome.message.body:
Welcome to OSHI. Your messages are end-to-end encrypted, and you signed up without a phone number or an account — nobody was told you are here.

OSHI also works with no internet at all: nearby phones over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and kilometres away with a LoRa radio.

Questions, or something broken? Tap below and write to me directly.
